tip: ни ... ни (ni ... ni = neither ... nor) still needs не on the verb. не знаем (ne znaem = we do not know) keeps the double negative English drops.
One sentence, two verb forms. строили (stroili) shows the building in progress, построили (pastroili) marks it finally completed.
ехал (ekhal = was riding) is the vehicle verb. Russian picks ехать (ekhat) for wheels and идти (idti) for on foot, a split English does not mark.
о (o) becomes об (ob) before a vowel sound: об этом (ob etam = about this), but о книге (o knige = about a book).
Russian wishes drop into the genitive: сладких снов (sladkikh snov = sweet dreams) literally means of-sweet-dreams.
A feminine direct object usually takes -у/-ю: интересную книгу (interesnuyu knigu = interesting book), changed from книга (kniga).
Playing a game uses играть (igrat) plus в (v): играет в шахматы (igrayet v shakhmaty = plays chess).
Toasts use за (za) plus the accusative: за ваше здоровье (za vashe zdarovye = to your health).
много (mnoga = many) forces the genitive plural: много туристов (mnoga turistav = many tourists).
Location after в (v) uses the prepositional case: в большом городе (v balshom gorade = in a big city).
Third person needs свой (svoy) for one's own: свою жену (svayu zhenu = his own wife); using его (yevo) would mean another man's wife.
себя (sebya = oneself) keeps one form for every subject: береги себя (beregi sebya = take care of yourself).
Russian time counts toward the next hour: половина десятого (palavina desyatava = half of the tenth) means 9:30, not 10:30.
Floors take на (na), not в (v): на пятом этаже (na pyatam etazhe = on the fifth floor).
From five up, the counted noun goes genitive plural: пять тысяч рублей (pyat tysyach rubley = five thousand roubles).
Rain uses the motion verb идёт (idyot = goes): дождь идёт (dozhd idyot = it is raining), literally the rain walks.
After когда about the future, Russian keeps future tense where English uses present: когда будете уходить (kagda budete ukhadit = when you leave).
зимой (zimoy = in winter) is instrumental with no preposition; seasons show 'in' by case alone.
Passive past uses был (byl = was) plus a -н form: был основан (byl asnovan = was founded).
After sense verbs like пахнет (pakhnet = smells), Russian uses an adverb, not an adjective: пахнет замечательно (pakhnet zamechatelna = smells wonderfully).
Exclamations use какой (kakoy = what a), agreeing with the noun. Neuter здание (zdaniye = building) takes the neuter form какое (kakoye).
Feelings put the person in the dative: мне холодно (mne kholadna = I am cold), literally to-me cold. Also тепло (teplo = warm), грустно (grustna = sad).
With понравился (panravilsya = appealed) the thing liked is the subject and the liker goes in the dative: отцу понравился ресторан (attsu panravilsya restaran = to father appealed the restaurant).
нужен (nuzhen = needed) agrees with the thing needed, not the person: masculine телефон (telefon = phone) gives брату нужен телефон (bratu nuzhen = brother needs).
много (mnoga = many) is followed by the genitive plural: много проблем (mnoga prablem = many problems), not the plain plural проблемы (prablemy).
Clock times use в plus the accusative number: в одиннадцать (v adinnadtsat = at eleven). No extra word for at is added beyond в.
на углу (na uglu = on the corner) is a street corner outside; в углу (v uglu) is an inside room corner. Same noun угол (ugal), different preposition.
о (o = about) becomes об before a vowel sound: об интересном фильме (ob interesnam filme = about an interesting movie).
Names use зовут (zavut = they call), a they-form with no subject: как вас зовут (kak vas zavut), literally how you they-call = what is your name.
без (bez = without) takes the genitive: без хорошего образования (bez kharoshevo abrazavaniya = without a good education).
